key_insight: Introducing token-level multi-heads restores the expressivity that linear attention loses (preventing global-context collapse) while preserving the efficiency advantages of linear attention.
problem_solved: Linear attention methods are efficient but often degrade model performance because they collapse global context or lose multi-head expressivity; prior fixes add extra modules that re-introduce costly computation.
method: Token-level multi-head mechanism: apply lightweight, per-token multi-head projections to recover head-wise expressivity without global quadratic operations.
Architectural design preserves linear time/space scaling by keeping core attention computations in a linearized form and using compact reweighting per token.
Avoids heavy auxiliary modules (e.g., depthwise separable convolutions), achieving a clean trade-off between expressivity and efficiency.
impact: Makes linear-attention Transformers practical for large-scale or resource-constrained deployments by restoring performance close to standard attention without losing computational benefits. Useful for practitioners needing scalable attention with strong representational power.
visual_elements: Two-panel diagram comparing standard quadratic attention vs linear attention: complexity arrows (O(N^2) vs O(N)) and a callout showing 'global-context collapse' in simple linear attention.
Architecture block showing token-level multi-head module inserted into a linear-attention block, highlighting per-token heads and lightweight reweighting.
Bar chart or scatter plot mockup illustrating trade-off: accuracy (or expressivity) vs compute/memory for standard, naive linear, and MHLA.
Icon strip: stopwatch (efficiency), brain/weights (expressivity), network graph (global context), and a shield/check (robustness/avoiding collapse).
paper_title: MHLA: Restoring Expressivity of Linear Attention via Token-Level Multi-Head
paper_authors: Kewei Zhang, Ye Huang, Yufan Deng, Jincheng Yu, Junsong Chen
